Rule: Each non-background object is a plus shape of 1s with a rectangular "pattern strip" attached on one side, extending away from the plus. Each strip is periodic along its axis; the output rewrites the whole strip span (fixing any off-period cells) and extends it with the same period/phase from the plus out to the grid edge, overwriting background and other strips but never 1-cells (plus shapes); overlapping extensions are applied in reading order (later objects win).

Key verifications: Pair 1 reproduces exactly (vertical 4/2 strip phase-extends to row 0, overwriting the horizontal strip's cell at (5,10) with 4, since object 2 is processed after object 1). Pair 2 reproduces exactly (the [2,3] strip extends to the bottom row, the [4,2] strip extends to the top row). On the test input: object 2's strip [[2,5],[7,3]] extends upward (even rows get [7,3], odd rows [2,5] for rows 0–12), object 3's strip [[2,4],[3,5]] extends down so row 24 cols 14–15 become [2,4], and object 1's already-full strip is regularized, correcting the two off-period cells at rows 23–24 cols 3–4 from [6,3],[4,2] to [4,3],[6,2].
